title: Leaving George Wein for the World's Greatest Jazz Band
summary: Freeman leaves Wein for the cooperative World's Greatest Jazz Band, staying six years touring warm places and Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And then, of course, I left George -- I remember the call. I got a call from George to do something. You know, George, I have been with you for 14 years, but I've got a chance now to go into a cooperative band that's going to be financed, that of course, being the World's Greatest Jazz Band which I talked about earlier, and George said, 'Well, that's fine, I wish you all the best.' But Ruby was not very happy with me for having done so because we did have this nice little group.

And anyway, I went into it and I stayed in it for six years, and we played, as I told you earlier, we never spent a winter in the north. We were in Hawaii, we were in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we were in Florida, we were in the Bahamas. We were in the Virgin Islands.

We traveled well and we went to Europe two or three times. We -- it was a very good life, I must say, for six years and then as I mentioned earlier, in the piece where you suggested we were getting too far ahead of ourselves, I was here with them in Europe four years ago, almost four years ago, and then got the opportunity, the offer to say and so I am here.
